info.name: EZ-Shop API
info.description:
Complete Postman collection for the EZ-Shop Express/Mongoose API.

## Base URL
Set per environment. `baseUrl` already includes the `/api` prefix.
- Local: http://localhost:7777/api
- Deployed: https://ez-shop-server.onrender.com/api

## Auth
Access token is a JWT returned in the response body as `data.token` (15 min lifetime). Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
The refresh token is an httpOnly cookie named `refreshToken` (7 days): login sets it, `GET /user/refresh` rotates it. Postman stores cookies automatically, so `GET /user/refresh` works right after login without extra setup.

- `POST /user/login` -> stores `accessToken` and `userToken`.
- `POST /admin/login` -> stores `adminToken`.
- The Admin folders override collection auth with `{{adminToken}}`.
- Public catalog reads explicitly opt out of auth.

## Response envelope
Success: `{ "success": true, "message": "...", "data": <payload>, "pagination"?: {...} }`
Validation failure (400): `{ "success": false, "message": "Validation failed", "data": { "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "details": [{ "field", "message" }] } }`
Other errors: `{ "success": false, "message": "...", "data": { "code": "API_ERROR" | "UNAUTHORIZED" | "INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR" } }`

## Rate limits
- Global: 1000 requests / 15 min per IP (header `RateLimit-Limit`).
- Auth endpoints (signup, login, verify OTP, forgot-password, reset-password): 10 / 15 min per IP. Running the auth folder repeatedly will start returning 429.

## Gotcha: route ordering inside /api/product
`/featured`, `/best-sellers`, `/filter`, `/search`, `/facets` and `/similar/:id` are registered before `/:slug/:id` and `/:id`. A product id must be a 24-char ObjectId, so a non-ObjectId segment falls through to the 404 handler.

## IDs
Variables such as `productId`, `categoryId`, `cartItemId`, `addressId` and `orderId` are captured automatically by the test scripts of the requests that create or list them. Run those first, or paste values into the collection variables.

exec: // Collection-level smoke check: every JSON response must carry the envelope.
// The invoice PDF download is the only non-JSON response, so guard on Content-Type.
pm.test('response uses the { success, message, data } envelope', function () {

request.description: Liveness probe. Response: `{ success, message, data: { status, uptime } }`.
Creates an unverified user and emails a 6-digit OTP. Returns 201 with `{ sent: true }` — no token yet. Verify with `POST /user/verify-signup-otp`. Rate limited to 10 per 15 min per IP.
Exchanges the emailed OTP for an access token. Sets the `refreshToken` cookie and stores the token in `accessToken` / `userToken`. OTP must be exactly 6 digits.
Customer login. Returns the user object spread with `token`, and sets the httpOnly `refreshToken` cookie. Stores the token in `accessToken` and `userToken`. Rate limited to 10 per 15 min per IP.

exec: pm.expect(pm.cookies.has('refreshToken'), 'refreshToken cookie missing — run POST /user/login first').to.be.true;

request.description: Rotates the access token using the httpOnly `refreshToken` cookie. No body and no Authorization header — the cookie is the credential, so it only works in the same Postman session that ran `POST /user/login`.
Revokes the refresh session server-side and clears the `refreshToken` cookie.
Emails a password-reset token. Returns `{ sent: true }` regardless of whether the address exists, to avoid account enumeration. Rate limited to 10 per 15 min per IP.
Consumes the reset token from the email. `newPassword` must be 8-128 characters. Rate limited to 10 per 15 min per IP.
Starts the Google OAuth flow. Sets a `state` cookie and issues a 302 to accounts.google.com. Open it in a browser, not the Postman runner — there is no JSON response.
OAuth callback. Google calls this directly; it is listed only for completeness. It validates the `state` cookie, sets the `refreshToken` cookie and redirects to the client.
Current customer profile. Requires `accessToken` — run `POST /user/login` first.
Partial profile update. All fields optional, but at least one is required. Note the route is `PATCH /api/user` (mounted at `/`), not `/api/user/profile`.
Change password while signed in. Both passwords must be 8-128 characters.
Admin login. Stores the token in `adminToken`, which every Admin folder uses. Rate limited to 10 per 15 min per IP.
Emails an admin password-reset token. Rate limited to 10 per 15 min per IP.
Consumes the admin reset token. Field is `password` here, not `newPassword` as on the customer route.
Signed-in admin profile. Uses `adminToken`.
Partial admin profile update. `name` and `phone` only, at least one required.

Paginated listing. Returns full documents (not projected) populated with `category`.

Query params: `page` (>=1, default 1), `limit` (1-100, default 10), `search`, `publish` (`true`/`false`), `isFeatured`, `isNewArrival`, `gender` (`men`/`women`/`unisex`), `category` (a single category id).

Captures `productId` and `productSlug` from the first item.

Storefront filter endpoint. Only ever returns published products and projects just the card fields (`name`, `slug`, `image`, `tag`, `price`, `discountPrice`, `rating`, `reviewsCount`, `category.name`, `variants.colorCode`) — deliberately not full documents, the payload is ~6 KB for 12 items vs ~37 KB for the same page from `GET /product`.

All params optional: `search`, `category` (comma-separated ObjectIds), `gender` (comma-separated), `type` (comma-separated subset of `New`, `Featured`, `Sale`), `price` (`min-max`, e.g. `100-500`), `size` (comma-separated), `color` (comma-separated), `sort` (`price-low` | `price-high` | `newest` | `featured` | `rating`, default `newest`), `minRating` (1-5), `page`, `limit` (1-100, default 20).

Invalid enum values are rejected with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.
Multi-facet example. Comma-separated `size`/`color` become `$in` queries on `variants.sizes.size` / `variants.color`; `price` applies to `discountPrice` OR `price`.

Available filter options derived from the live catalogue (single `$facet` aggregation over published products). Returns `{ price: { min, max }, sizes: string[], colors: [{ label, hex }], ratings: number[] }`.

The storefront fetches this once and caches it for 5 minutes. Sizes come back in wearing order (XXS..XXXL, then numeric).
Up to 8 published products flagged `isFeatured`, populated with `category.name`.
Up to 6 published products flagged `isBestSellers`.
Quick typeahead search. Matches `name` with a case-insensitive regex. `name` is required and `limit` is 1-50 (default 10). This endpoint does not filter on `publish`.
Up to 4 other published products in the same category. Registered before `/:slug/:id`, so `similar` is never mistaken for a slug.

Canonical product-detail route. If the slug no longer matches the stored slug (e.g. the product was renamed) the response is `{ product, redirectUrl: "/<slug>/<_id>" }` instead of `{ product }` — the client is expected to follow it. Run `GET /product` first to populate `productSlug` and `productId`.
Fetch a single product by ObjectId. Returns 404 API_ERROR when it does not exist.

formdata.value: A product created from the Postman collection.

request.description:
multipart/form-data (required — the route has `upload.fields([image, variantImages])` before validation).

`image` (max 1) and `variantImages` (max 50) are optional files uploaded to Cloudinary.

`variants` and `variantImageMap` are sent as JSON **strings** and parsed by the schema:
`variants`: `[{ color, colorCode, images[], sizes: [{ size, stock, sku, price, discountPrice }] }]`
`variantImageMap`: `[{ variantIndex, count }]` — assigns `count` of the uploaded `variantImages` to `variants[variantIndex].images`.

Required: `name`, `description`, `price` (>0), `stock` (>=0), `category` (ObjectId). Optional: `discountPrice`, `image`, `slug` (auto-slugified from `name` when omitted), `gender` (default unisex), `tag` (default New), `publish` (default true), `isFeatured` / `isBestSellers` (default false).

Run `GET /category` or create a category first so `{{categoryId}}` is populated.
Partial update, also multipart. At least one field is required. Renaming updates the slug automatically. Replacing `variants` replaces the whole array — it is a JSON string here too.
Deletes the product and returns the deleted document. Note this does not remove Cloudinary assets or existing order line items.

Public category list, paginated (`page` >= 1, `limit` 1-100, default 10). Served from a 5-minute in-process cache that is invalidated on any category write — expect ~13 ms when warm. Captures `categoryId` from the first item.
Single category by ObjectId.
Admin only. multipart/form-data because of `upload.single("image")`. `name` and `slug` are required; `image` is an optional file. Clears the category cache. Captures `categoryId`.
Admin only, multipart. At least one field required. Uploading a new `image` deletes the previous Cloudinary asset. Clears the category cache.
Admin only. Deletes the category and its Cloudinary image. Products referencing it keep a dangling `category` id.
The signed-in customer's cart. Captures `cartItemId` from the first line item when present.
Cheap line-item count for the header badge.

Adds a product to the cart. `productId` is required (ObjectId); `variantId` and `size` are optional but must be sent together for variant-level stock. `quantity` is 1-10, default 1.

Run `GET /product` first so `{{productId}}` is populated.
Sets the absolute quantity for a line item (1-10). Not a delta. `cartItemId` comes from `GET /cart` or the add response.
Empties the cart. Registered before `/:cartItemId`, so `clear` is never treated as an id.
Removes a single line item.
The customer's wishlist ids.
Wishlist with populated product details.
Adds the product if absent, removes it if present. There is no separate add/remove endpoint.
All saved addresses for the signed-in customer. Captures `addressId`.

Creates an address. Required: `label` (`Home` | `Work` | `Other`), `name` (letters only), `phone`, `addressLine1`, `zipCode` (digits), `state`, `city`, `country`. Optional: `addressLine2`, `isDefault` (default false). Captures `addressId`, which the checkout requests need.
Partial update. At least one field required; the same field rules as create apply to whichever fields you send.
Deletes the address.
Public paginated reviews for a product (`page` >= 1, `limit` 1-100, default 10). Captures `reviewId` from the first review.
The signed-in customer's own review for a product, so the UI can prefill the edit form. Registered before `/:productId`.
Creates a review. `productId` (ObjectId) and `rating` (integer 1-5) are required; `comment` is optional. One review per user per product — a second attempt is rejected.
Updates your own review. At least one field required.
Deletes your own review.

Public discount quote so guests can preview savings. Uses `optionalAuth`: if a valid `accessToken` is present the per-user usage limit is also checked. `code` is uppercased and validated against `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` (2-32 chars); `subtotal` must be >= 0. Returns the computed discount, or an error when the code is expired, inactive, below `minOrderValue` or used up.
Admin only. Paginated coupon list with optional `search`.
Admin only. Single coupon by ObjectId.

Admin only. Required: `code` (2-32 chars, letters/digits/`-`/`_`, uppercased automatically), `type` (`percentage` | `fixed`), `value` (>0).

Rules: `percentage` value cannot exceed 100, and `maxUsesPerUser` is only allowed on `percentage` coupons (sending it on a `fixed` coupon is a 400).

Optional: `description`, `minOrderValue`, `maxDiscountAmount`, `maxUses`, `maxUsesPerUser`, `expiresAt`, `active`.
Admin only. Partial update; the code itself cannot be changed. At least one field required.
Admin only. Deletes the coupon. Already-placed orders keep their recorded discount.

Places a cash-on-delivery order from the signed-in customer's cart, using a saved address. `addressId` (ObjectId) and `deliveryMethod` (`standard` | `express` | `same-day`) are required. Stock is verified before the order is written, and the cart is cleared on success.

Requires a non-empty cart — run `POST /cart` first. Captures `orderId`.

Guest checkout with no account. `products` is an array of `{ productId, variantId?, size?, quantity }` (at least one, quantity 1-10); `address` is a full inline address; `deliveryMethod` is required; plus contact `name`, `email`, `phone` at the order level. Point your Stripe CLI at `POST /api/webhook` to see the order flip to paid.
Admin only. Paginated orders. Optional `search`, `orderStatus` (`processing` | `shipped` | `delivered`) and `paymentStatus` (`pending` | `paid` | `failed`). Captures `orderId`.
Admin only. Aggregate dashboard counters. Registered before `/:id`.
The signed-in customer's order history, paginated. Uses `accessToken`.
Looks an order up by Stripe checkout session id — used by the success page after redirect. `optionalAuth`: signed-in owners see the full order, guests get the public subset.
Order lookup by id with `optionalAuth`, for the guest order-confirmation page.
Authenticated order detail. Uses `accessToken`; ownership is enforced.
Admin only. `orderStatus` (`processing` | `shipped` | `delivered`) and/or `paymentStatus` (`pending` | `paid` | `failed`); at least one required.
Admin only. Deletes the order record. Note this does not restock the items.

Starts a Stripe Checkout session for the signed-in customer's cart. Same body as `POST /order/cod`. Returns the session (including its id and redirect URL) and captures `sessionId`. Requires a non-empty cart.
Stripe Checkout for a guest. Same body as `POST /order/guest`.
Invoice data for an order you own. Uses `accessToken`.
Streams the generated PDF invoice. In Postman use **Send and Download** — the response is `application/pdf`, not JSON, so the collection-level envelope test will fail on this one.
Public newsletter signup. Only `email` is required; re-subscribing an existing address is idempotent, not a 409.
Admin only. Paginated subscriber list.
Admin only. Paginated users with optional `search` (max 120 chars) and `role` (`User` | `Admin`). Captures `userId`.
Admin only. Per-customer dashboard detail (orders, totals). Registered before `/:id`.
Admin only. Single user by ObjectId.
Admin only. Deletes the user. Their orders and reviews remain.

header.description: Generated by Stripe. The handler verifies it against STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and returns 400 without a valid one.

request.description:
Stripe webhook. Receives the **raw** body (`express.raw`, mounted before `express.json()`), verifies the `stripe-signature` header and, on `checkout.session.completed`, marks the order paid, sets it to `processing` and clears the buyer's cart.

You cannot hand-craft a working signature. Test it properly with the Stripe CLI:
```
stripe listen --forward-to localhost:7777/api/webhook
```
This request is included for reference only; it returns 400 as shipped.
